transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I keep going back over my jobs again and again. I’ll check the breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—sometimes I even drive back to a site to check something. A simple install ends up taking way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.
When you feel the need to go back and check, is it because an unwanted thought keeps popping into your mind that something is wrong?

Yeah. Even when I know I checked the panel or the disconnect, I get this thought that maybe I missed a loose neutral or left something that could start a fire. I try to push it aside, but it keeps coming back, even after I’m home.
When you go back to check, does checking make the anxiety ease up, even if only for a little while?
Yeah, it eases up for a little while after I check. Then it starts creeping back in, and I feel like I have to go over it again—breakers, labels, photos, all of it.
Do these repeated checks feel excessive or unreasonable to you?

Yeah, I mean, part of me knows I’ve already checked it and it should be fine. But I still end up going back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—sometimes even driving back to the site. It takes way longer than it should, and people are noticing.
Do these thoughts about having missed something feel intrusive and unwanted?

Yeah. I don’t want them there. I’ll know I checked the panel, but then the thought barges in that I missed a loose neutral or left something that could start a fire. I try to shake it off, but it follows me all the way home.
Besides checking, do you have any other repetitive behaviors or mental rituals that you feel driven to do?

Mostly it’s the checking. I keep going back through the breakers, labels, torque marks, and the photos, sometimes more than once. If I still don’t feel settled, I’ll even drive back to the site. It turns a straightforward job into something that takes way too long.
About how much time in a day do these checking thoughts and repeated checks take up?

It can take up a big chunk of the day, especially on a job. I keep going back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, and photos, and sometimes I end up driving back to the site. A simple install takes way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.
Outside of these checking episodes, do you generally see yourself as a perfectionistic person who likes things done in a very exact way?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I like doing my work right, but I haven’t thought of myself as someone who needs everything exact in general.
Outside of your work checking, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many other parts of life?
I’m not sure I do. I haven’t really noticed myself worrying a lot about other areas of life the same way.
Did these checking thoughts and behaviors start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
I can’t point to one specific event or change that started it. It feels like it kind of built up over time, but I’m not completely sure.
When the thought comes up that you may have missed something, do you believe it’s probably true, or do you recognize it’s most likely not true even though it still feels hard to ignore?

I know I checked it, so I guess I know it’s probably not true. But then the thought comes back—maybe there was a loose neutral or something I missed that could start a fire—and I can’t just let it go. It follows me home.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a traumatic event related to electrical work, like a fire, serious injury, or near-miss?
No, I can’t think of anything like that happening to me or that I’ve witnessed.
Have these checking thoughts and repeated checks caused problems for you at work or in your daily life?

Yeah. Jobs that should take one visit end up taking longer because I keep going back over things or making extra checks. My schedule’s slipping, and I think it’s starting to affect clients’ confidence in me and the time I have to spend with the apprentices. And after work, I’ve been skipping stuff I used to enjoy because I’m still thinking about a job or wondering if I need to go back.
If you try not to check, do you feel a strong urge that makes it hard to resist?

Yeah, very strong. If I try to leave it alone, I keep thinking I need to go back through the breakers, the labels, the torque marks, check the photos again. Sometimes I end up driving back to the site just to look one more time. It’s hard to resist because I don’t feel settled until I’ve checked.
When you check again, is it mainly to relieve the anxiety from the thought that you missed something?

Yeah. I’m trying to get rid of that feeling that I might’ve missed something. I’ll go over the breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—sometimes I’ll even drive back to the site—until I feel like I can finally leave it alone.
